name: SL-164
summary: SL-164, also known as dicloqualone or DCQ, is an analogue of methaqualone developed in the late 1960s by a team at Sumitomo. SL-164 has similar sedative, hypnotic and properties to the parent compound, but was never marketed for clinical use, due to higher risk of convulsions. Like other 4-substituted analogues, such as methylmethaqualone, SL-164 may cause seizures.

summaryZh: SL-164是一種含氮有機氯化合物，分子式C16H12Cl2N2O，為安眠酮的結構類似物，1960年代由住友集團的科研團隊開發。
summaryZhHans: SL-164是一种含氮有机氯化合物，分子式C16H12Cl2N2O，为安眠酮的结构类似物，1960年代由住友集团的科研团队开发。

sideEffects.en: It was never marketed because it carried a higher risk of convulsions than methaqualone. Its parent drug methaqualone causes sedation, poor coordination and dependence, and overdose can be dangerous.
sideEffects.zh: 它從未上市，原因是引發抽搐的風險比甲喹酮更高。其母體藥物甲喹酮會造成鎮靜、協調變差與依賴，過量可能很危險。
sideEffects.zhHans: 它从未上市，原因是引发抽搐的风险比甲喹酮更高。其母体药物甲喹酮会造成镇静、协调制差与依赖，过量可能很危险。

fact.en: Its other name, dicloqualone, reflects the two chlorine atoms added to the structure of methaqualone, the sedative once sold as Quaalude.
fact.zh: 它的另一個名稱dicloqualone，反映出它是在甲喹酮（曾以Quaalude之名販售的鎮靜劑）結構上多加了兩個氯原子。
